reason: E1 provides thermodynamic ranking supporting Al2O3/SiO2 stability over Mn oxides, and E4 shows Al2O3/Cr2O3 formation in Al-containing HEA, but no cited evidence directly demonstrates that Si or Al reduces cation diffusion, limits stress, or prevents cracking in CrFeCoNiX, nor that Mn oxides cause spallation in this system; the mechanistic claims about diffusion, stress, and adherence are largely inferred rather than supported by the cited passages.
premises: Al and Si form thermodynamically stable, slow-growing oxides (Al2O3, SiO2) that limit cation diffusion and stress
Mn forms less protective, volatile oxides leading to rapid growth and stress accumulation
Cr2O3 contributes to a protective scale when combined with Al2O3 or SiO2
Thermodynamic stability of oxides (Al2O3 > SiO2 > MnO > Cr2O3) governs protective scale formation
Oxide adherence and stress control determine cracking/spallation resistance
